axes.label: Craft & polish
axes.description: Visual quality, typography, colour, composition, motion feel, finish. Would a discerning person believe a human designed this on purpose?

axes.label: Technical ambition
axes.description: How hard is what was actually built, and is it built correctly? Real technique versus the cheapest thing that looks similar.

axes.label: Brief adherence
axes.description: Did it do everything the prompt asked, completely, including the output contract? Stubs and TODOs count against.

axes.label: Originality
axes.description: Is the idea and its execution distinctive, or is it the median AI answer to this prompt?

The Clear button is dead: `onclick="clear()"` inside an inline handler resolves to the deprecated no-op `document.clear` before reaching the global function, so clearing the canvas silently does nothing.

Footer text ('Watch patterns emerge') advertises behaviour the implemented rules cannot produce given the mutation rate.

Canvas sizing is not robust: `COLS` and `ROWS` are computed once and never rebuilt on resize, while the canvas dimensions are changed. This can leave an incorrectly sized simulation region after resizing.
The canvas ignores device pixel ratio, so it will render soft on high-DPR displays.
Simulation speed is coupled to refresh rate (`step()` occurs every second animation frame) rather than elapsed time, so behavior differs materially between 60 Hz and 120 Hz displays.
